'''Mary Ellen Tracy''' (aka '''Sabrina Aset''') (born 1943) is the [[high priest]]ess of the '''Church of the Most High Goddess''', who was convicted in 1989 of a single [[misdemeanor]] count of running a house of [[prostitution]] in connection with the operation of the church, located in [[West Los Angeles]], [[California]]. Tracy is a graduate of the [[University of Miami]], cum laude in chemistry, did graduate work in chemistry at [[UCLA]], and received her masters in [[Environmental Sciences]]/[[Chemistry]] from [[Portland State University]].

==The Church==
According to Mary Ellen and Wilbur Tracy, the couple – both former devout and dedicated [[Mormons]] – created and founded the [[Kemetism|Modern Egyptian]] [[neo-pagan]] Church of the Most High Goddess following a [[Divinity|divine]] [[revelation]] received at an oceanside cottage in [[Santa Monica]], California, in the year 1984. In testimony later given in a [[Los Angeles]] superior court, Wilbur Tracy described "a brilliant light," through which "knowledge was being poured in without voice." Tracy further claimed that [[God]] appeared to her as an old man, with flowing white beard and long white hair.

<blockquote>On April 24, 1984, in broad daylight, I had a revelation that changed my life and the way I perceive the world and others. However, because I was blinded by the ignorance of the modern education, which I foolishly accepted as knowledge, I did not immediately understand the full impact of the revelation. I failed to understand that the mind can perceive only what the mind can conceive. What I experienced was beyond my conception, while my perception was completely distorted by what I had been taught was enlightenment. It was only when I set aside my prejudices – those beliefs which I had been conditioned to accept as fact, but which were in fact false – that I began to understand the experience.<ref>[http://www.goddess.org/vortices/wheregods.html ''Where Are The Gods?'' by MaatRaAh] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100815030314/http://www.goddess.org/vortices/wheregods.html |date=2010-08-15 }}</ref></blockquote>

As a result of their alleged divine experience, Mary Ellen and Wilbur Tracy founded the Church of the Most High Goddess, with precepts based on their own research into ancient [[Ancient Egypt|Egyptian]] practices. Tracy, a [[classical scholar]] in her own right, assumed the role of High Priestess of the church, whose [[Divinity|divine]] duties included engaging in [[sexual intercourse]] with [[wikt:congregation|congregants]]. According to Tracy herself, she had sex with over 2,000 men as part of a ritual of spiritual cleansing.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.watchman.org/cults/sexgodss.htm|title=Sex Goddess In Court|work=Watchman Expositor|volume=6|year=1989|publisher=[[Watchman Fellowship|Watchman Fellowship ministry]]|access-date=2012-03-28}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=http://articles.latimes.com/keyword/mary-ellen-tracy | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023092353/http://articles.latimes.com/keyword/mary-ellen-tracy | url-status=dead | archive-date=October 23, 2012 |title=In the News: Mary Ellen Tracy | work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref><ref name="google3">{{cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=348&dat=19890910&id=-WUvAAAAIBAJ&pg=3783,2105299 |title=Rome News-Tribune - Google News Archive Search |access-date=2015-07-19}}</ref> In a post on her church's website, Tracy, who is bisexual, stated that she had had sexual contact with thousands of men and women over the course of her religious activities.<ref name="goddess2">{{cite web|url=http://www.goddess.org/sabrina/index.html |title=What Do You Call a Female Stud? |author= Sabrina Aset, High Priestess of the Church of The Most High Goddess |publisher=goddess.org|access-date=2015-07-19}}</ref>

As a result of her various legal difficulties, Mary Ellen Tracy was asked to permanently discontinue her voluntary work with the ''Placerita Canyon Nature Center'' in [[Newhall, Santa Clarita, California|Newhall]], California.<ref name="latimes">{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-01-13-me-1216-story.html |title=NEWHALL : Convicted Prostitute Loses Nature Center Post|date= January 13, 1993|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|access-date=2015-07-19}}</ref>

During the late 1980s, ''The Newhall Signal'', a [[daily newspaper]] published in [[Los Angeles County]], presented a series of articles about the Church of the Most High Goddess, founded by Mary Ellen Tracy and her husband Wilbur Tracy, where sexual acts played a fundamental role in the church's sacred rites.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Padilla |first1=Steve |title=Woman Tells Court She Performed Sex Acts for Religious Reasons |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1989-08-31-me-1666-story.html |website=Los Angeles Times |access-date=13 June 2020 |date=31 August 1989}}</ref> The articles aroused the attention of local law enforcement officials, and in April 1989, the Tracy's house, located at 6601 West 5th St, Los Angeles,<ref>{{Cite book |last=California (State) |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=reuO_ODSnlQC&q=6601 |title=California. Court of Appeal (2nd Appellate District). Records and Briefs: B046140, Petition for Writ |language=en}}</ref> was searched and the couple arrested on charges of [[pimping]], [[Procuring (prostitution)|pandering]] and [[prostitution]]. They were subsequently [[convicted]] in a trial in [[State court (United States)|state court]] and sentenced to jail terms: Wilbur Tracy for 180 days plus a $1,000.00 fine; Mary Ellen Tracy for 90 days plus mandatory screening for [[Sexually transmitted disease|STDs]].<ref name="nytimes">{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1990/05/02/us/religion-based-on-sex-gets-a-judicial-review.html?pagewanted=1 |title=Religion Based on Sex Gets a Judicial Review - NYTimes.com |date= May 2, 1990 |work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=2015-07-19}}</ref><ref name="google2">{{cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1454&dat=19911225&id=lwEzAAAAIBAJ&pg=2917,3256597 |title=Star-News - Google News Archive Search |date=December 25, 1991 |access-date=2015-07-19}}</ref>

==Film and television==
During the early 1990s, Mary Ellen Tracy hosted her own [[public-access television]] talk show series, ''Sabrina On ... ''. She has also appeared in a number of [[x-rated]] films under a variety of stage names, including the ''Positively Pagan'' series, and ''Club Head 2'' (1991). On January 29, 1992, Mary Ellen Tracy was featured on a [[television broadcast]] of ''[[Phil Donahue Show|Donahue]]'',<ref name="google4">{{cite book|title=In Therapy We Trust: America's Obsession with Self-fulfillment|author=Moskowitz, E.S.|date=2001|publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press|isbn=9780801864032|url=https://archive.org/details/intherapywetrust00mosk|url-access=registration|page=[https://archive.org/details/intherapywetrust00mosk/page/261 261]|access-date=2015-07-19}}</ref> as well as ''[[The Montel Williams Show]]'', appearing with such other [[New-Age]] spiritualists as [[Aidan Kelly]], First Officer of the ''Southern California Local Council of the [[Covenant of the Goddess]]'', and Avilynn Waters of the ''Los Angeles Nest of the [[Church of All Worlds]]''.
